flags.title: The release-readiness board states a page count that is 22 pages stale
flags.detail: Row RR-01 of ledger/readiness.json says '116 published HTML pages'. Measured on this tree: 160 published, 150 excluding this namespace and the board's own output page. RR-01 has no {measure} token, so unlike RR-03, RR-05 and RR-10 nothing recomputes the number when the tree moves.
flags.why_it_matters: The board exists to answer 'which of Amazon's stated requirements does this site meet today'. A row whose evidence is a stale count is a row a reader cannot check, on the one page whose job is to be checkable.
flags.close_action: Add a {published_pages} measure to tools/build_readiness.py and replace the typed number in RR-01 with the token.
flags.owner: owner (an agent session with tools/build_readiness.py and ledger/readiness.json in scope)

flags.title: The canonical suggestion board carries the same proposal twice (SG-11 and SG-12)
flags.detail: SG-11 and SG-12 share an area, a title and near-identical body text. The board's own derived counts therefore report 12 suggestions where 11 distinct proposals exist, and the release-readiness board's RR-03 and RR-09 both point at SG-12 while RR-03 and RR-09 are the same gap.
flags.why_it_matters: The brief asks for a board where the owner chooses a path. A duplicated row is a path offered twice, and the owner cannot tell whether choosing one discharges the other.
flags.close_action: Delete one row and repoint RR-03 / RR-09 at the survivor, or merge the two into one row with the union of their options.

flags.title: Fourteen operator and companion pages still describe the site as 'AI-powered'
flags.detail: 25 occurrences across 14 pages; the exact phrase 'AI-powered Amazon affiliate' on 11. The T55 rebuild removed it from every reader-facing page on 2026-11-16; what remains is the operator surfaces (console/, research-hub/, summary.html, review-trace.html) and two companion prototypes (affiliate-lab/, zone2/).
flags.why_it_matters: It is the single strongest signal that the copy was produced from a brief rather than from the work. It also invites exactly the reading of the site that Google's scaled-content-abuse policy describes, for no benefit: no reader chooses an affiliate site because it is AI-powered.
flags.close_action: Remove the phrase from the operator and companion pages. Describe what the pages do (sourced rows, blanks left blank) rather than what built them.
flags.owner: owner — this is a copy decision, and it is proposed as DB-01 on the design board

flags.title: Zero of 138 published pages carry an Associates tag, so no page on the site can currently earn
flags.detail: Measured with Amazon's published tag format (NAME-NN). The three supplied short links resolve without a tag parameter. Amazon's own application-review page states that the tags 'must be embedded in your Amazon product links on the site(s) declared in your application', and that the application is checked once at least three qualifying sales have been driven within the first 180 days.
flags.why_it_matters: This is the finding the brief's 'so real people can click the links and buy' runs into. Until a tag exists, traffic cannot convert into qualifying purchases, and without three of them the application is never reviewed. Everything downstream — conversion data, the optimizer, the revenue model — is blocked behind one string the owner has to supply.
flags.close_action: Supply the Associates ID (tag) and the marketplace; then rebuild the links with it.
flags.owner: owner — carried on the canonical register as F-07 and F-24, and asked as BQ-02 on the questions register

flags.title: 43 pages across seven companion namespaces carry no canonical URL

The remaining 43 sit entirely in preserved companion namespaces (research-hub 12, affiliate-lab 10, zone2 8, audit 6, revalidation 6, northstar 1, release 1). tools/build_head_meta.py --audit reports them rather than failing them, by design.
flags.why_it_matters: It is the owner's open decision (MQ-08 / DS-12), not a defect. It is recorded here because 'which surface is the site' has to be answered before an application lists a URL.
flags.close_action: Decide which surface is the declared Site, then either fold the companions into the head contract or exclude them from the declared set.
flags.owner: owner — open decision, carried as MQ-08 and DS-12
